newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end lower, calm ahead of strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end lower, calm ahead of strike.

text.p: Colombian stocks drifted to a lower close on a correction in blue chips, while the market showed little stress in the face of a planned public sector strike scheduled for midnight.
Bogota's IBB index fell 0.17 percent to 1,021 in 1.3 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general index lost 0.59 percent to 15,790.92 in 1.8 billion pesos.

"The indices carried on with their downward slide as the price correction continued, following the rapid rises at the start of the year. Tomorrow we will be working as if it were just a normal day," said one Bogota broker.
"Of course there may be a psychological factor that pushes down volume in the markets, but this strike will not have any real structural effects on the economy," the broker added.

Colombia's stock exchanges are not known for drastic reactions to political or labor news. Most of the top stocks are held by just a few investors, many of them executives of the companies in which they hold shares.

On the Bogota exchange, brewing giant Bavaria fell 0.23 percent 6,360. Banco de Colombia, meanwhile, gained 0.71 percent to end at 420 pesos after falling back at the end of last week on lower 1996 profits.

"Maybe the stock and fixed-income markets will be a little quiet tomorrow because of the psychological effect of the strike. Some people may have difficulty in getting to work," another Bogota broker said.

"There would, however, only be a structural effect if the government caved in to the workers' demands, because it would create fiscal problems and send a bad sign to investors who would then pull out," he added.
On the Medellin exchange, cement manufacturer Cemento Argos fell 0.72 percent to 6,900 and another cement maker, Cementos Caribe dived 2.5 percent to 5,489.
Banco Industrial Colombiano fell 2.68 percent to 3,450, while Banco Bancoquia tumbled 3.25 percent to 2,800.
